Look up the next-state distribution after a pathway

Source: R/query.R
query_pathway.Rd

query_pathway() returns the probability distribution that the fitted tree assigns to the next state after a given history, or the probability of one particular next state. For example, it gives the probability of Disengaged after the history Active, Average, read directly from the fitted model.

By default the history need not be a context of the tree: as in prediction, the longest suffix of the history that is in the tree is used, falling back to the root when no suffix matches. With exact = TRUE only a context of the tree is accepted, and other histories return NA. To find which context matched, use predict.transitiontrees() with tidy = TRUE; to test whether a pathway is a context, use pathway_exists().

Usage

query_pathway(tree, pathway, next_state = NULL, exact = FALSE)

Arguments

tree

A transitiontrees object.

pathway

The history, oldest state first: a single string in arrow notation ("A -> B") or a character vector (c("A", "B")). "(start)" or an empty vector denotes the root.

next_state

A state whose probability is returned. NULL (default) returns the whole distribution.

exact

Require pathway to be a context of the tree. Default FALSE (use the longest matching suffix).

Value

With next_state, a single probability. Otherwise a named numeric vector with one probability per state, in the order of the tree's states. NA for a pathway that is not a context when exact = TRUE.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input when tree is not a fitted tree or next_state is not one of its states.

See also

pathway_exists(), subtree(), predict.transitiontrees(), tree_pathways().

Examples

tree <- context_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 3)
query_pathway(tree, "Active -> Average")
#>     Active    Average Disengaged 
#>    0.37500    0.51875    0.10625 
query_pathway(tree, c("Active", "Average"), next_state = "Disengaged")
#> [1] 0.10625
